title: Compote de Reinettes Blanches (White Pippin Apple Compote)
description: Prepared with apples, lemon juice, and water.
steps: You peel some apples and you cut them in half, after having removed the skin
You put them in an earthenware vessel where there is water and a lemon juice, so that they keep their whiteness

You clarify a half pound of sugar; as soon as the syrup is well clarified, you throw the apple halves in the sugar; take care to turn the apples; when you feel the fork sink in them, you will remove them from the syrup
Pass the syrup through a silk sieve, and make it reduce; you will boil it again; then you will pour it on the apples; serve them cold or hot
If you want to decorate them, take the skin of a red calville apple, and make a design on the halves

title: Compote de Verjus (Verjuice Compote)
description: Prepared with verjuice, water, and sugar.
steps: Split each grain with the tip of a small knife to remove the seeds
Once all seeds are removed, throw them into water ready to boil
When the verjuice begins to pale, remove from heat and add a half-glass of cold water
Leave it in the same water until it is cold so it has time to turn green again
Put a fish of water with six ounces of sugar in a pan to boil
Add all the verjuice at once and let it boil two or three times
Take care to skim
Arrange your verjuice in the compote dish before putting the syrup on the verjuice
Reduce the syrup if it is too clear

title: Compote grillée de Poires (Grilled Pear Compote)
description: Prepared with pears, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: pears for cooking that are not very ripe
ingredients.sourceText: pears for cooking that are not very ripe

steps: Place pears in a well-lit good oven until the entire skin is well burnt, turning them carefully so they grill equally
Continue until the skin comes off by rubbing them in water
Remove the skin this way, cut them in half and remove the seeds
Rinse them again in several waters
Put them in a pot to cook with a chopine of water, a small piece of cinnamon, and a quarter pound of sugar
Cover the pot and cook them until they soften greatly under the fingers
Reduce the syrup and serve them hot if you wish

title: Compote of Green Apricots and Green Almonds (Bourgeoise)
description: Prepared with apricots or almonds, water, and sugar.
steps: Boil water in a pan with two handfuls of soda; when it has boiled twice, throw your apricots or almonds into the pan
When they have boiled once, remove them with a skimming spoon and rub them well in your hands to remove the down, and as you do so throw them into fresh water
Have fresh boiling water ready in another pan to cook your apricots
You will see when they are cooked enough by pricking them with a pin; if it enters easily and the apricot falls by itself, it is a sign they are cooked enough
Remove them in fresh water, then boil sugar in your pan and put your apricots or almonds in it
Let them boil gently on a small fire until they are well green, and serve
Alternatively, some do not make lye for their apricots or almonds, they merely rub them with salt to remove the down, and then blanch and cook as described above

title: Confiture de Campagne (Country Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with wine and fruit or pears or apples or quinces.
steps: Take sweet wine called mou, you cannot make it too sweet, take as much as you need for the amount of fruit you want to make preserve with, put it in a copper pot or pan and boil it over a clear fire until the fruit is ready to be set aside.
Take the fruit you want to preserve (pears, apples, or quinces), cook it in water until softened, then peel it and put it in your sweet wine syrup, and let it boil until it is cooked.

Be sure to skim during cooking. You will know when it is done by putting some of the syrup on a plate; if you see it remain ruby-colored and does not run when you tilt the plate, that is proof you must remove your preserve.
Put it in pots and cover when cold. It matters not whether the sweet wine is white or red.

ingredients.name: Currants, one pound of fruit per pound of sugar

Remove your preserve from the fire, pass it through a sieve and put it immediately into pots
When it is cold, cover your pots, dip your first paper in brandy so the preserve keeps better
Never cover the pots except when the preserves are cold

title: Confiture de Prunes (Plum Preserve)
description: A fruit preserve made with plums and sugar.

ingredients.name: Plums (such as Perdigon, Reine Claude, Mirabelle, or other varieties)
ingredients.sourceText: Plums (such as Perdigon, Reine Claude, Mirabelle, or other varieties)

ingredients.name: sugar per hundred plums
ingredients.sourceText: Five pounds of sugar per hundred plums

steps: Blanch the plums
When they are soft to the touch, remove them with a skimmer and place them in fresh water
Clarify five pounds of sugar for every hundred plums
Place the plums one by one in a clean vessel so they do not crush, and add the sugar slightly warmer than lukewarm

For four or five days, morning and evening, drain the plums on a sieve and boil the sugar, skimming it each time, then return the plums to the vessel with the sugar poured over, always slightly warmer than lukewarm
The Reine Claude plums should remain green, and other plums should keep their color
At the end, if the sugar is not syrupy enough at the final cooking, cook it further by adding two glasses of water to degrease it, then pour it boiling hot over the plums

ingredients.sourceText: Sugar, one pound per pound of fruit

steps: After you have removed the down from the apricots or almonds as marked previously for green apricot compotes on page 481, make them cook in water in the same manner until by pricking them with a pin it enters easily and the apricot falls by itself

Boil your sugar for four or five consecutive days, morning and evening, without your fruit, which you put to drain on a sieve
Put it back in a terrine and pour your sugar over it, which must be only slightly more than lukewarm
When your apricots and almonds are well green, your preserve will be made

title: Confitures de Groseilles (Currant Preserves)
description: A fruit preserve made with currants, water, and sugar.
steps: Separate the currants from the stems so the wood of the stems does not give a bitter taste
Place them in a pot with a glass of water
When they have boiled a few times and burst, place them in a horsehair sieve
Pass the juice a second time over the pulp so it is very clear
Squeeze it to extract all the liquid
For thirty pounds of juice, clarify thirty pounds of sugar and bring it to the crack stage
Pour the juice over the sugar and boil for a quarter hour
Skim well and pour into pots
Or put the currant juice on the fire and add sugar in pieces
Let the preserves boil well and skim
Place a few drops on a plate and tilt it to see if the preserve sets
You can use only three-quarters of a pound of sugar per pound of fruit, but the preserves must cook longer
If using cassonade, it must be clarified

title: Confitures de Groseilles à la Bourgeoise (Currant Preserve Bourgeois Style)
description: A fruit preserve made with currants and sugar.

ingredients.name: Sugar, clarified, equal measure to the juice
ingredients.sourceText: Sugar, clarified, equal measure to the juice

steps: Clarify your sugar as explained previously on page 540
String the currants and put them in the pan
Make them melt on the fire by letting them boil once or twice
Put them afterwards to drain on a sieve
Measure your currant juice and put as many pints of clarified sugar in another clean pan that you will cook to the crack stage

You will know its cooking stage by means of a goblet full of water that you will hold in your left hand, wet the upper fingers of your right hand that you will quickly dip into your sugar, and then into the goblet, and if the sugar that stuck to your fingers dries and is brittle, you will put your currant juice into it
Make two boils covered and skim well
Put your jelly into your pots

title: Consommé (Consommé)
description: A soup made with beef, hens, and broth.

ingredients.name: Eight or ten pounds of sliced beef
ingredients.sourceText: Eight or ten pounds of sliced beef

steps: Take eight or ten pounds of sliced beef, eight old hens, two calf necks, four calf knuckles
Put your meat in your pot
Fill it with great broth
Make it skim
Be careful to refresh your broth three or four times to make the foam rise well
After make your consommé boil gently
Garnish your pot with carrots, turnips, onions, three cloves
When your meats are cooked, pass your consommé through fine cloth or a silk sieve so that your consommé is very clear
Do not add salt if you moisten it with great broth

title: Coulis Bourgeois (Bourgeois Stock)
description: Prepared with lard, veal, and onions.

ingredients.name: flour and butter per half-septier
ingredients.sourceText: One tablespoon of flour and butter per half-septier

steps: Put small pieces of lard and veal round in the bottom of a casserole according to the quantity of coulis desired; for good coulis, use one pound per half-septier
Add two or three onions and as many root vegetables
Cover the casserole well and cook over low heat so the meat has time to release its juices
Then increase the heat until the meat is ready to brown
Lower to low heat so the meat browns gently to the casserole, creating a good gratin
Remove the meat and vegetables to a plate
Put a piece of butter and flour in the casserole according to the quantity of coulis desired, about one tablespoon per half-septier
Cook over heat until the roux is beautiful
Add hot bouillon
Return the meat to make it cook for another two hours over very low heat; degrease the coulis often
When finished, pass it through fine cloth or a sieve for use

title: Croquettes d'Agneau (Lamb Croquettes)
description: Prepared with lamb, lamb or meat, and veal.

ingredients.name: a lamb leg or other lamb meat
ingredients.sourceText: a lamb leg or other lamb meat

ingredients.name: three whole eggs and two yolks
ingredients.sourceText: three whole eggs and two yolks

steps: Cook a lamb leg on the spit or other lamb meat that has been roasted
Cool and remove the meat
Remove skin and nerves; cut the meat into small dice
Take some lamb fat, cut into small dice, and mix with the meat
If no fat available, use cooked veal udder
Add cooked mushrooms cut into small dice
Add a little grated nutmeg and coarse pepper
Take six spoonfuls of velvet sauce and four spoonfuls of aspic, mix together
Reduce the sauce by more than half; it must be somewhat thick
When reduced, add a liaison of three egg yolks
Stir the sauce on fire without leaving it so the liaison does not break
When the sauce is bound, add butter the size of an egg and melt while stirring well
Check seasoning and pass through a sieve over the meat
Stir well when the sauce is added
Cool the ragout
Stir it and place spoonfuls on a tile, successively until finished, making eighteen or twenty portions
If the ragout is not cold enough, let it cool further to make it workable
Take the portions and place breadcrumbs on a table
Shape as desired: pear-shaped, ball-shaped, oval or elongated
Roll well in breadcrumbs
Beat three whole eggs and two yolks with a little fine salt and coarse pepper like an omelet
Dip the croquettes in the egg so it covers all sides
Place in breadcrumbs and ensure they are well breaded so they do not dissolve in frying
Leave on a tile
Just before serving, put frying oil on the fire
When very hot, place the croquettes in it
When colored, remove and drain on white linen
Dress in a pyramid and fry a little parsley

description: Prepared with rabbits, breadcrumbs, and butter.

steps: Roast three young rabbits on the spit
Remove the fillets and the largest part of the thighs
Cut the meat into small dice, removing nerves and skin
Place the meat in a casserole with one small spoonful of béchamelle
Reduce the béchamelle to almost half
Add butter the size of an egg to the sauce without placing it on the fire, allowing it to melt
Pass the sauce through a sieve over the rabbit meat

Roll them in breadcrumbs
Dip them in beaten eggs with a little salt and coarse pepper
Ensure the eggs coat all the croquettes
Roll them again in breadcrumbs, ensuring they are well coated all over to prevent them from bursting
At the moment of serving, put them in fairly hot fat
When they have a nice color, remove them and drain on white linen
Fry a handful of parsley and place it on top of and around the croquettes
If you do not have béchamelle, reduce velouté into which you put a liaison of three eggs

title: Croquettes de Morue (Cod Croquettes)
description: Prepared with cod, cream, and breadcrumbs.
steps: When your cod is cooked, cut it into dice and put it in a saucepan.
Add butter the size of two eggs, one small tablespoon of flour, a little salt, pepper, a little grated nutmeg, and half a glass of cream.
Place your sauce on the fire and stir until it comes to a boil.
Pour it over your cod, mix it well with the sauce, and let it cool.
Divide it into fifteen or twenty portions and shape your croquettes into an agreeable and uniform form.
Coat them with breadcrumbs.
Break four or five eggs, season them, beat them, and dip your croquettes in them; coat a second time with breadcrumbs.
An instant before serving, place your frying oil on the fire; when it is very hot, put your croquettes in it, and as soon as they have a nice golden color, remove them.
Place them on a white napkin, arrange them in pyramids, and put fried parsley on top.

title: Crème au Café (Coffee Cream)
description: Prepared with coffee, egg yolks, and water.
steps: Put three half-setiers of water in a coffee pot.
When it boils, add {{source-1}}, stir with a spoon and return it to the fire to boil until it rises four or five times.
Let it settle to draw it off clearly and put it in a saucepan with one chopine of milk and a piece of sugar.
Make it boil until only the amount you need for the size of your dish remains.
Mix five egg yolks with a pinch of flour, then add the cream.
Pass it through a tamis to pour into the serving dish, which should be on a saucepan with water ready to boil.
Cover with a saucepan lid with a little fire on top.
Let it boil until the cream is set.
Serve hot.

title: Crème au Caramel (Caramel Cream)
description: A confection made with cream, lemon, and egg yolks.
steps: Put in a saucepan one chopine of milk, one half-setier of cream, with a small piece of cinnamon, a good pinch of coriander, the zest of green lemon, and bring to boil for a quarter-hour
Remove from the fire, and put in a small office pan one quarteron of sugar with one half-glass of water
Make it boil on a stove until it reaches caramel, that is to say, the color of dark cinnamon
Remove from the fire and add the cream to it; return to the fire until the sugar is dissolved with the cream
Then dilute five egg yolks with a pinch of flour, add the cream to it, pass it through a sieve to cook it in a bain-marie as the previous ones

title: Crème au Petit Pain (Small Bread Cream)
description: A bread preparation made with cream, coffee, and egg yolks.
steps: Take three small coffee rolls, remove the bottom crust so you can remove the crumb without damaging the top crust, soak the top and bottom crusts with milk and sugar

In a saucepan, put two small spoonfuls of flour which you will dilute with seven egg yolks (set the whites aside in a basin), put with the yolks three crushed macarons, chopped green lemon, a piece of sugar, a chopine of cream; cook everything on the fire for a quarter-hour and remove it
Remove the small rolls from the milk to drain them

Put the dish you must serve on, put this cream in the bottom, the bottom of the rolls on top, take the tops of the rolls; in place of the crumb you removed, put cream in it, and put them in the dish as if they were whole, cover them on top with the same cream, finish them on top so that each roll keeps its shape
Cook them in the oven or under a covered pie dish for half an hour
Take egg whites which you whip into snow and put sugar into it

Remove the small rolls from the oven to cover them with these whipped egg whites while always preserving their shape, put fine sugar on top, and put them back in the oven until they are a beautiful yellow color, and serve

description: Prepared with cream, tea or tarragon or celery or parsley, and egg yolks.

ingredients.sourceText: tea or tarragon or celery or parsley as desired

steps: Put in a saucepan one half-setier of cream and one chopine of milk, nearly one quarteron of sugar
Bring to boil and reduce by a third
If it is a tea cream, add enough tea to make five cups; let it boil a moment and pass through a sieve

If you wish to make a tarragon cream, take two branches of tarragon that you will boil for half a quarter-hour in water, and then put it to boil in the cream; leave it only long enough to give the taste, and remove it promptly, for fear the taste does not dominate
Do the same for celery and parsley cream
The cream being passed through a sieve, dilute five egg yolks with a pinch of flour, and cook it in a bain-marie as the coffee one

If you wish to serve them cold, put no eggs or flour in them; after they are passed through a sieve and the cream is lukewarm, dilute rennet or chopped chicken gizzard skins in it, pass it through a sieve and put it in the dish you must serve, which you put on some hot ashes; cover with a lid in which you also put some hot ashes, leave until the cream is set, and put it in the cold until you serve

title: Crème à la Moèlle (Marrow Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, marrow, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: a little green lemon, chopped very finely
ingredients.sourceText: a little green lemon, chopped very finely

steps: Dilute eight egg yolks with two small spoonfuls of flour, a little finely chopped green lemon, a little orange flower water, two half-setiers of cream, and a piece of sugar
Take a quarter-pound of marrow which you melt on the fire and pass through a sieve, and put this marrow into the cream
Cook this cream on the fire for half an hour, then remove it
Whip the eight egg whites that you set aside and mix them well into the cream, and arrange it in the dish you must serve

Cook it in the oven or under a covered pie dish as the previous one; when it is cooked, take a glazer or some clean feather which you dip in good hot butter, and pass it lightly over the cream, put nonpareille immediately on top (these are small dragées of all colors), and serve

title: Crème à la Vanille Renversée (Inverted Vanilla Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, vanilla, and egg yolks.
steps: Fill a mold or small molds with cream
Bring the cream to a boil
Add sugar and vanilla
Allow to boil several times and then cool
If the mold holds a pint, use 12 egg yolks and 3 whole eggs mixed with the cream
Pass five times through cheesecloth
Lightly butter the mold and pour the cream into it
Place in a bain-marie to set, ensuring the water does not boil vigorously
Place fire on the mold cover but not too intense
Test if set by placing a finger in the center of the cream
When ready to serve, invert the mold onto a plate
Heat the remaining cream and turn it like a white sauce
When the cream coats a wooden spoon, remove from heat
Turn it briefly and pour over the inverted cream

title: Cuisses d'Oie à la Purée (Goose Thighs with Puree)
description: Prepared with fat, lard, and carrots.
steps: Lift six fat goose thighs
Debone them to the interior joint
Season with salt and coarse pepper
Place some chopped lard where the bone was
Reassemble the meat and sew them, giving them a nice shape
Place lard rinds in a casserole
Place the thighs there and cover them with lard rinds
Add three carrots, four onions, two bay leaves, a little thyme, two cloves, and one spoonful of bouillon
Braise for two hours
At service time, drain them and remove the thread
Dress them on your dish and mask them with your puree; if you wish, you can put a puree of lentils, or of green peas, of onions, and Robert sauce, tomato sauce

title: Cuisses de Dindons Accompagnées (Turkey Legs with Accompaniment)
description: Prepared with turkey, sweetbreads, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: coulis or beurre manié with flour
ingredients.sourceText: coulis or beurre manié with flour

steps: Blanch the calf's sweetbreads in boiling water and cut them into large cubes with many mushrooms also cut into cubes
Combine them with grated lard, chopped parsley, chives, basil, shallots, salt, coarse pepper, and two egg yolks
Take two raw, well-cleaned turkey legs and bone them completely except for the end bone attached to the leg
Fill the legs with the sweetbread mixture and sew them shut so nothing escapes
Cook them in a braise made with one glass of white wine and an equal amount of good broth, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and a little salt
Cover with lard strips and cook over low heat
When cooked and little sauce remains, degrease it, remove the lard strips and bouquet
Add two spoonfuls of coulis to bind the sauce, or if you have none, add a piece of butter worked with a pinch of flour and a little blanched chopped parsley
Thicken over the fire and serve on the legs with lemon juice or verjuice

title: Cuisses de Dindons à la Crème (Turkey Thighs in Cream Sauce)
description: A sauce made with turkey, lard, and chives.
steps: If using raw turkey thighs, lard them crosswise with thick lard
In a casserole, combine butter mixed with flour, salt, pepper, parsley, chives, garlic, shallots, cloves, bay leaf, thyme, basil, and coriander
Add half a septier of milk and bring to a boil
Place the turkey thighs in the mixture and boil on very low heat
When the thighs become tender under the fingers, remove and drain them
Take the fat from the cooking liquid and dip the thighs in it
Bread them immediately and grill on low heat, lightly basting with the remaining fat
In a casserole, heat half a glass of juice with two spoonfuls of verjuice, salt, and pepper
Serve the sauce under the thighs

title: Cuisses de Lapereau au Soleil (Young Rabbit Legs au Soleil)
description: Prepared with rabbit, bouillon, and velouté.

ingredients.name: Medium lardons, seasoned with salt, pepper and pounded aromatic herbs
ingredients.sourceText: Medium lardons, seasoned with salt, pepper and pounded aromatic herbs

steps: After boning your legs, lard them closely with medium lardons seasoned with salt, pepper and pounded aromatic herbs.
Put butter in a casserole; heat it a little, and put your legs in it.
Place them on a hot stove; sauté them for ten minutes.
Add about one spoon of flour and one pot spoon of bouillon, two spoonfuls of velouté to degrease, a bay leaf, some mushrooms, half a bottle of good white wine, and a bouquet of parsley and chives.
Cook over high heat to make the liquid reduce.
Be careful to degrease your ragout.
When it is cooked and reduced, add a liaison of five egg yolks and a small piece of fine butter.
Place your twelve legs on a platter to cool; drizzle them with their sauce.
When they are cold, remove the bone of the foreleg, soak them well in their sauce, and put them in breadcrumbs one after the other.
Place them on a platter.
Break five whole eggs; add a little fine salt and a little coarse pepper.
Beat your eggs as you would for an omelet.
Dip your legs in it; make sure they are coated all over.
Roll them in breadcrumbs; give them a pleasing shape.
Put them on a platter; at the moment of serving, you fry them.

title: Cuisses de Lapereau en Chipolata (Young Rabbit Legs in Chipolata Sauce)
description: A sauce made with rabbit, bouillon, and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: 2 small pot spoons of bouillon, strained through a silk tamis
ingredients.sourceText: 2 small pot spoons of bouillon, strained through a silk tamis

ingredients.name: Mushrooms, sautéed in water and lemon juice
ingredients.sourceText: Mushrooms, sautéed in water and lemon juice

steps: Bone your legs as in the previous recipe.
Throw them into boiling water for two minutes; then remove them and trim them.
Put {{source-1}} in a casserole; place your legs in it.
Sauté them for ten minutes.
Then pour 1 and 1/2 spoonfuls of flour, which you blend with your butter.
Add about 2 small pot spoons of bouillon strained through a silk tamis.
Turn your ragout until it boils.
Add mushrooms sautéed in water and lemon juice to prevent them from darkening, a bay leaf, and a bouquet of parsley and chives.
Cook your ragout over high heat so it reduces.
Add small lard that you have blanched.
When your ragout is three-quarters cooked, add twenty small onions that you have blanched.
You can also add fifteen chestnuts not from Lyon.
Join six sausages, which you will tie in the middle with string so they are not too long.
Put them in boiling water for five minutes; after refreshing them, put them in your ragout.
Be careful to degrease it well.
When it is cooked, add a liaison of four egg yolks.
Arrange your legs on your plate and your ingredients on top. Your ragout should be properly salted. You can serve this ragout in a tureen to serve as a flan.

description: Prepared with rabbit, lard, and veal.

ingredients.name: Small piece of lard to replace the bone
ingredients.sourceText: Small piece of lard to replace the bone

ingredients.name: Cucumbers à la crème, sautéed mushrooms, tomato sauce, game stock, or glaze sauce for serving
ingredients.sourceText: Cucumbers à la crème, sautéed mushrooms, tomato sauce, game stock, or glaze sauce for serving

steps: Bone the thighs down to the joint as with the previous ones
Lard them with fine lard
Season them on the inside
Put a piece of small lard in place of the bone
With a needle and thread, bring the flesh together and secure it
Put bards of lard in a casserole with a few slices of veal, two carrots, three onions, two bay leaves, and a little thyme
Place your thighs on top with seasoning
Cover them with a round of buttered paper
Pour in a full spoonful of bouillon
Simmer for an hour and a half, or more depending on the quality of your rabbit
Be careful to put fire on your lid
At the moment of serving, drain your thighs
Remove the trussing strings and glaze them
Place your chicory on your plate and your thighs on top
You may serve underneath cucumbers à la crème, a sauté of mushrooms, tomato sauce, game stock, or a glaze sauce

title: Cuisses de Lapin à la Purée de Lentilles (Rabbit Legs with Lentil Purée)
description: Prepared with rabbit, lentil, and lard.

ingredients.name: Medium lardons, seasoned with aromatic herbs, salt and pepper
ingredients.sourceText: Medium lardons, seasoned with aromatic herbs, salt and pepper

steps: Take rabbit legs; eight are sufficient for an entrée.
Bone them, that is, remove the bone up to the joint of the foreleg; try not to cut the top.
Lard the inside of your legs with medium lardons seasoned with aromatic herbs, salt and pepper. Since the leg is generally very dry, put many lardons in it.
When they are well larded, throw them into boiling water for two minutes.
Remove them, trim them, and put lard strips in a casserole with a few slices of veal, two carrots, two onions, a bay leaf, and a little thyme.
Place the legs on this seasoning. Cover them with lard strips and a round of buttered paper.
Pour about one small pot spoon of bouillon with a little drippings from the cooking pot.
Let them simmer for two hours, more or less, depending on how tender your rabbit is.
At the moment of serving, drain them. Arrange them on your plate and mask them with a lentil purée.

Take cooked forcemeat the size of fresh eggs with an equal amount of mushroom purée

title: Cuisses de Poulets au Soleil (Chicken Thighs in the Sun)
description: Prepared with chicken, bay leaf, and onion.

ingredients.name: Twelve chicken thighs from good chickens
ingredients.sourceText: Twelve chicken thighs from good chickens

ingredients.name: One onion studded with a clove
ingredients.sourceText: One onion studded with a clove

steps: Break the bone of each thigh up to the inner joint and cut off the large end at the leg.
Put a good piece of butter in a casserole and heat it gently.
Arrange the thighs in it so they take on a beautiful shape.
Add salt, coarse pepper, a bay leaf, an onion studded with a clove, and a bouquet of parsley and scallions.
Place them over high heat and sauté until well browned.
Add a spoonful of flour and a pot-spoon of hot bouillon along with mushrooms.
Boil for three-quarters of an hour.
Degrease the ragout before the time expires.
When removing the thighs, the sauce should be reduced to three-quarters of its volume.
Remove the bouquet, onion, and bay leaf.
Add a liaison of three egg yolks.
Arrange the thighs on a platter with sauce on top.
When they are cold, coat them well with their sauce.
Roll them in breadcrumbs, then dip in beaten and seasoned eggs.
Coat them again with breadcrumbs, making sure they are well covered everywhere.
At serving time, place them in hot oil.
When they have a beautiful color, drain them on white cloth.
Arrange them in a crown shape.
Fry a good handful of parsley and place it in the center.

description: Prepared with chicken, truffles, and lard.

ingredients.name: Twelve chicken thighs from fine fat chickens
ingredients.sourceText: Twelve chicken thighs from fine fat chickens

steps: Prepare twelve chicken thighs as you would for a bigarrure.
Chop eight peeled truffles.
Grate half a pound of lard and put it in a casserole with three spoonfuls of good oil.
Add your chopped truffles, a little four spices, a little salt and coarse pepper.
Pass them over heat briefly, then let them cool.
Stuff your chicken thighs with this mixture.
Sew them with needle and thread so the truffles do not escape.
To give them a pleasant shape, insert a leg bone through the thin end of the thigh.
Put lards of bacon in a casserole, arrange your thighs on top, and cover them with lard.
Add your truffle scraps and cook covered.
Three-quarters of an hour before serving, place your thighs over heat.
At that moment, drain them.
Remove the thread and arrange them in a crown shape.
Place a sauté of truffles in the center.

title: Culotte de Bœuf à l'Anglaise (Beef Rump English Style)
description: Prepared with beef, carrots, and parsnip.

ingredients.name: farce of godiveau or other meat farce
ingredients.sourceText: farce of godiveau or other meat farce

steps: Take a cut of beef of the size you judge appropriate and tie it
Put it in a pot proportioned to its size with two or three carrots, one parsnip, three or four onions, a bouquet of parsley and chives, one clove garlic, three cloves, one bay leaf, thyme, and basil
Moisten with bouillon or water, season with salt and pepper
Cook at low fire in court bouillon
At half the cooking time, prepare small cabbage heads: take a large cabbage, remove the greenest leaves, and blanch it whole in boiling water for half an hour
Remove it to fresh water and press it firmly without breaking the leaves
Remove the leaves one by one and put a little farce of godiveau or other meat farce inside
Stack three or four leaves together as you fill them, one on top of the other, to form small cabbage heads slightly bigger than an egg
Tie them and cook them with the beef
When cooking is done, drain everything and wipe it of its fat
Arrange the beef in the serving dish, cut each cabbage head in half, and arrange them around the beef with the cut side out
For the sauce, take some of the cooking liquid, pass it through a sieve, degrease it, add a little coulis to bind it, reduce it over the fire to sauce consistency
Serve on the meat and on the cabbage heads

title: Céleri au Velouté (Celery in Velouté Sauce)

steps: Peel, wash, and cut the celery into small sprigs, leaving the tender leaves

Drain it well as you would for chicory
Chop it as you would chicory
Put a piece of butter in a casserole with the celery, a little salt, coarse pepper, and a little grated nutmeg
Pour 3 spoonfuls of velouté and as much bouillon over it
Reduce it until it is thick enough to serve
Place croutons around it
If you do not use velouté, when the celery is drained, add a small spoonful of flour mixed with the celery, moisten with bouillon as you would for chicory

description: Prepared with celery, sauce, and consommé.

ingredients.name: butter, the size of an egg

When they have boiled 20 minutes, refresh them and drain
Trim again and place in a casserole with a little coarse pepper, an egg-sized piece of butter, 4 spoonfuls of Spanish sauce, and 6 spoonfuls of consommé
Cook on a fairly hot fire
Let it boil for half an hour
Arrange on a plate with the sauce underneath
Alternatively, make a light roux, moisten with bouillon, turn the sauce until it boils, then pour it over the celery and finish as described above

title: Côte de Bœuf Braisée (Braised Beef Rib)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and veal.
steps: Trim your rib well
Clear the end of the bone
Lard it with large pieces of lard seasoned with four spices, salt, and pepper
Put strips of lard in the bottom of your casserole
Over your lard strips, put slices of veal and beef, fourteen carrots, five large onions, one of which is studded with three cloves, two bay leaves, a little thyme, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Tie with string, arrange your rib in this braise
Cover it with lard and put your vegetable garnishes on top
Add two spoonfuls of bouillon
Bring your braised rib to a boil, then put it on a low fire so it simmers gently for three hours; less if your rib is tender
When it is cooked, drain it and remove the string
Pass a little of the cooking liquid through a silk sieve
Degrease it and reduce it
Glaze your rib and pour your reduced liquid underneath

steps: Cut and trim your chops as you would mutton chops

When they are stiffened on one side, turn them over
Leave them a moment on the fire; when they resist under the finger, remove them
Have a piquant sauce ready
At the moment of serving, drain your chops, dip them in your sauce, and dress them in a crown
Pour your sauce underneath

Add a small spooonful of bouillon, a little salt, fine pepper, a dash of vinegar, and a bay leaf
Reduce your sauce a little, pass it through cheesecloth, and serve it for your chops

title: Côtelettes de Veau sautées (Sautéed Veal Cutlets)
description: Prepared with veal cutlets, shallots, and salt.
steps: Cut the cutlets rib by rib, ensuring they are all the same thickness
Trim them so they are rounded at the thick end of the meat and squared off at the bone side
Trim the bone to the size of half an inch
Place salt and coarse pepper on your sauté pan or skillet
Put your cutlets in the pan with fine salt on top and a little coarse pepper
If you wish to sauté them with fine herbs, sprinkle finely chopped parsley and finely chopped shallots on top
Melt half a pound of fine butter and pour it over your cutlets
At the moment of serving, place them on a hot fire
When they are cooked on one side, turn them to the other side
Avoid letting your fire brown the cutlets
Press your finger on the meat; if you feel the meat is still soft, it is not cooked enough; you would need to turn them and remove them from the hot fire so they cook more gently
When they are cooked, arrange them in crowns on the plate
Remove the butter that is in your sauté pan or skillet
Put in about four spoonfuls of espagnole sauce and a little glaze
Detach the glaze produced by your cutlets and put your sauce in the plate

If you have no sauce, leave a little butter; put a little flour which you stir with your stock; put a little bouillon in it, a little fine herbs; make it boil; sauce your cutlets and check if they are of good taste

title: Côtelettes de Veau à la St-Gara (Veal Cutlets Saint-Gara Style)
description: Prepared with veal cutlets, tongue, and lard.

ingredients.name: Mushrooms, chicory, tomato sauce, or cucumbers (optional garnishes)
ingredients.sourceText: Mushrooms, chicory, tomato sauce, or cucumbers (optional garnishes)

steps: Cut and trim the cutlets as in previous recipes.
Cut the scarlet tongue into medium lardons.
Grate some lard and warm it, then sauté the lardons in it.
Add grated nutmeg and fine pepper to the lardons.
Let the lardons cool and lard the cutlets through and through.
Put a piece of butter in a large casserole and firm up the cutlets to trim them more correctly.
In the casserole, place strips of lard, parings of tongue, a little laurel, a little basil, and a few slices of ham.
Place the cutlets on this seasoning, cover them with lard.
Add two or three carrots cut into slices, or four onions cut into slices, and fill with two glasses of consommé or bouillon.
Cook the cutlets on low heat for two hours.
Put fire on top of the lid.
At the moment of serving, drain and glaze the cutlets.
Pass the cooking liquid through a silk sieve.
Add three spoonfuls of large Spanish sauce to a casserole.
Add four spoonfuls of the cooking liquid from the cutlets.
Reduce the sauce by half.
Arrange the cutlets on the platter and add the reduced sauce.
If you do not have sauce, make a light roux and moisten with the strained liquid, add two spoonfuls of jus for color, and reduce by one-third.
Ensure the sauce is not too salty and add a little coarse pepper.
You may serve under these cutlets a sauté of mushrooms, chicory, tomato sauce, or cucumbers.

title: Daube d'Oie (Braised Goose)
description: Prepared with goose, lard, and chives.
steps: Scald the goose and pluck it; make it refirm on the fire, and pluck it again

Lard it throughout with lardons of seasoned lard kneaded with parsley, chives, two shallots, half a clove of garlic, all chopped fine, a bay leaf, thyme, basil chopped to a powder, salt, coarse pepper, and a little grated nutmeg
After having larded the goose, truss it and place it in a pot just fitting its size with two glasses of water, as much white wine, and half a glass of eau-de-vie, add a little salt and coarse pepper
Seal the pot well and cook over a very low fire for three or four hours
When cooked and the sauce is very reduced so that it can set in aspic, arrange the daube in its serving dish
When it is almost cold, pour the sauce over it, and serve only when it is completely set as a cold entremet

title: Des Gâteaux de Fleurs d'Oranges (Orange Blossom Cakes)
description: A cake made with orange, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: Sugar mixed with egg white, consistency of double cream

steps: Make a paper mold with white paper kept double and folded around to make a border two fingers high, like a box, of medium cake size
Put {{source-0}} in a pan with a glass of water
Boil and skim, continuing until, when dipping the skimming spoon in the sugar and blowing through the holes, large sparks fly out that hold together
Immediately add a quarterons of orange blossom petals and boil until the sugar returns to the point it was at when you added the flowers
Remove from the fire and stir quickly with a spatula, rubbing all around the pan and in the middle, until you see the sugar beginning to rise
Quickly throw in a little fine sugar mixed with egg white no thinner than double cream that you have ready
Stir quickly and pour your cake into the mold
Hold the bottom of the pan on the cake while it is hot, because this prevents it from falling
Violet cakes are made the same way, except that for a quarterons of violets only three quarterons of sugar are needed
Roasted orange blossom cakes are made the same way, except you roast the orange blossoms with a little fine sugar before putting them in the other sugar

title: Des Haricots Verds (Green Beans)
description: Prepared with green beans, bouillon, and egg yolks.
steps: Select very tender green beans and break off the small ends, then wash them and cook them in water
When cooked, drain the beans
In a saucepan, melt butter with chopped parsley and ciboule
Add the drained beans and toss them two or three times over the fire
Add a pinch of flour and a little good bouillon with salt, and allow them to boil until there is no more sauce
When ready to serve, add a liaison of three egg yolks mixed with milk, then a dash of verjuice or vinegar
Once the liaison has set on the fire, serve as an entremets
Alternatively, you may serve them in gravy by using coulis and veal juice instead of the liaison

steps: Begin several days in advance for best results
Singe the turkey lightly and clean it well
Gut it through the vent
Remove the breastbone
Wash and clean three or four pounds of truffles according to the turkey's size
Chop the truffle peelings finely or pound them
Scrape two pounds of lard and put it in a saucepan with {{source-3}} and {{source-4}} (clarified because otherwise it would give a sour taste to the truffles; it would be better not to use it then)
Add your chopped or pounded truffle peelings and your whole truffles, salt, coarse pepper, four spices, finely chopped parsley and finely chopped shallot
Put your saucepan on the fire
When your preparation boils, let it cook for ten minutes
Stir your truffles from time to time
Place them to cool
When they are set in the fat, put them in your turkey
If time permits, prepare it eight days in advance
When putting it on the spit, truss it and cover it with a bard of lard
Oil paper and wrap it
Secure your turkey on the spit so it does not turn, because your truffles would fall into the dripping pan
Half an hour before removing it from the spit, remove the paper and give it a fine color
If serving as a relevé, chop two or three truffles and pass them through a little butter, and add five spoonfuls of espagnole and two of consommé, a little four spices and coarse pepper
When your sauce is somewhat reduced and degreased, pour it in a sauce boat
For roasting it is served without sauce

title: Dindon en Daube (Turkey in Daube)
description: Prepared with turkey, lard, and veal.
steps: Pluck and gut the turkey
Cut off its legs and truss the thighs inside
Secure them with string and a trussing needle
Singe and clean it
Season large lardons with salt, pepper, four spices, and fine herbs
If you wish, lard the breast and thighs of your turkey as finely as possible
Put lard slices in a braising pan, your turkey on top, two veal knuckles, the turkey legs, four carrots, six onions, three cloves, two bay leaves, thyme, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Cover your turkey with lard slices and a piece of buttered paper
Moisten it with bouillon, four pot spoonfuls, more if the turkey is large, a little salt
Simmer for three and a half hours
When cooked, remove the braising pan from the fire; do not remove your turkey for half an hour after, so it does not break apart
Pass your cooking liquid through a fine cloth
Reduce it by a quarter, or more if it is too thin
Break an egg into a saucepan; beat it well, and pour the jelly into it; beat it well with your egg
Check if it tastes good; if it lacks flavor, add a little aromatic flavoring, some parsley leaves, some chive stems
Put it on the fire, stirring vigorously until it is about to boil
When it reaches its first boil, place it on the edge of the stove with a lid and fire on top
Let it simmer for half an hour
Then pass it carefully through a fine cloth and let it cool to serve around the daube

Pass it through a white cloth and add a little sugar

Take eight eggs and beat the whites separately, setting the yolks aside.
Using a spoon, poach two or three spoonfuls of the beaten whites at a time in the cream, forming poached eggs without yolks.
Drain them and stack them one on top of another until you have formed eight poached eggs.
Arrange them on the serving dish.
Put the cream on the fire to reduce it to the consistency of a sauce.
When ready to serve, add the eight yolks and thicken over the fire without boiling, to prevent them from curdling.
Arrange the sauce over the egg whites.

title: Emincé de Gigot de Mouton aux oignons (Sliced Leg of Mutton with Onions)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, onions, and sauce.
steps: Slice the meat from the leg of mutton as previously described
Cut twelve large onions in half, remove the head and tail
Cut them into slices forming half-circles, removing the core
Put a large piece of butter (about the size of an egg) in a pan
Pass the onions over a fairly hot fire
When the onions are golden, add three spoonfuls of Spanish sauce and three spoonfuls of consommé, a little coarse pepper and salt
Reduce the onion until slightly thick
Pour it over the sliced mutton, sauté to mix with the onion, and keep warm without boiling
Arrange when ready to serve with croûtons like the preceding ones

If sauce is not available, mix one half-spoonful of flour with the butter and onion, moisten with broth or water, add salt and coarse pepper, and when ready to combine with the sliced mutton, add a dash of vinegar

ingredients.name: Three or four pounds of sliced beef

ingredients.name: Two calf necks and one calf knuckle

steps: Put in a pot or saucepan (according to the quantity of empotage) three or four pounds of sliced beef, two calf necks and one calf knuckle, four old hens
Moisten this quantity of meat with two spoonfuls of broth
Put your pot on a stove and boil everything until it is reduced
Be careful that your empotage is not too colored; for this you must be careful that your sweating does not stick too much; make it a beautiful blond color
Then fill your pot with great broth and garnish it with vegetables such as carrots, turnips, onions
Do not add salt since your great broth is seasoned
Let your pot remain three and a half hours on the fire
When the meats are cooked, pass the broth of your empotage through fine cloth or a sieve
Try to make your broth very clear; you will use it to moisten all your soups

description: Prepared with snails, bouillon, and egg yolks.
steps: Put a good handful of ashes in a medium pot with river water and bring to a boil
Throw in the snails and leave for a quarter hour
When they come easily out of their shells, remove them to lukewarm water to clean
Place them again in clear water and boil for an instant, then drain
In a casserole, put a piece of butter with a bouquet of parsley, ciboule, one clove of garlic, two cloves, thyme, laurel, basil, and salt
Heat gently and coat the snails lightly with flour mixed with a little salt and pepper
Moisten with bouillon and a little white wine
Let cook until the snails are tender and the sauce is reduced
When serving, add three yolks of eggs mixed with a little cream and finely chopped parsley
Bind without boiling and add a little white mustard with a pinch of nutmeg

title: Esturgeon à la Matelote (Sturgeon in Matelote Style)
description: Prepared with bread crumbs, shallot, and chives.
steps: Cut bread crumbs into rounds the size of a small coin.
Pass them over the fire with butter until they are a beautiful golden color and let them drain.
Cut a piece of sturgeon into small slices, slightly thin.
Put them in a plate, arranged so they are not on top of each other, with a piece of butter, salt, and coarse pepper.
Cook them over low heat, and as they are cooked on one side, turn them to the other.
Cooking takes only a quarter hour.
Remove them from the plate and put a little flour in it, which you stir with the butter, and then add finely chopped shallot, parsley, and chives.
Moisten with two glasses of red wine.
Let the whole boil together for a quarter hour.
Put the sturgeon back in the sauce to heat it without boiling.
Throw in a little chopped capers.
Garnish the edges of the plate with your fried bread croutons, being careful to sprinkle them a little with sauce.

steps: Cut chicken breast whites into small dice

Cook them on a low fire for ten minutes
Drain your whites and let them cool
Put a piece of bread crumb in the same saucepan with bouillon and a little finely chopped parsley
Stir it with a wooden spoon, mashing and reducing it to a paste
When your bouillon is reduced and your bread crumb is well softened, let it cool
Have a cooked and cold veal breast; if not available, use butter instead
Pound your chicken whites; when well pounded, pass them through a quenelle sieve and set aside
Pound your bread crumb the same way, pass it through the sieve and set apart
Pound your veal breast, pass it through the sieve and set to the side
Make three equal portions of chicken whites, bread crumb, and veal breast
Pound it all together
When you have pounded it for three quarters of an hour, add five or six egg yolks according to the quantity of forcemeat
Pound your yolks with your forcemeat as you add them
When your forcemeat is made, remove it from the mortar and put it in a terrine
Use it as needed, either with butcher's meat, poultry, or game; use the same procedure and also employ this forcemeat for the gravies

title: Façon de Faire du Vinaigre Rouge, Blanc et Rozat (Method for Making Red, White, and Rose Vinegar)
description: Prepared with vinegar and wine.

ingredients.name: Clean wine suitable for making vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: Clean wine suitable for making vinegar

ingredients.name: Juice of ripe wild blackberries (optional, for color)
ingredients.sourceText: Juice of ripe wild blackberries (optional, for color)

steps: According to the quantity of vinegar you wish to make, take a vessel more or less large; to make twenty pints, take a barrel of that size that is new; if it is old wood, you must have it planed inside.
Take one pint of the strongest vinegar that you make boil, and put it boiling into the barrel, which you will plug well with the bung, and roll it while shaking until it is completely cold.
Six hours later, remove this vinegar and place the barrel in a warm location.
After having bunged it, make a hole in the top of the barrel above the jable, large enough to insert a large funnel.
Pour in through the funnel two pints of good vinegar.
Eight days later, add one pint of clean wine suitable for making vinegar.
Every eight days add one pint of wine until the barrel is half full, then you may add more.
You must take care that the wine is always of the same strength as the first that you put in, because if it were weaker, the increase you would make would not have the same strength.
Your barrel being full and the vinegar in its state, withdraw two-thirds of it which you put in another vessel.
Then you will gradually return wine to the barrel as described above; by this means you always have vinegar.

For white vinegar: put ten pints of vinegar on the fire and let it boil until it is reduced to eight; then have it distilled in an alembic, putting in more or less according to the quantity you desire.
For rose vinegar: dry an ounce of musk roses in the sun for two days, which you will put in one pint of vinegar; place the roses and vinegar in the sun for fifteen days in a well-stopped bottle.
For tarragon, elder, or carnation vinegar: make the same way; for orange flower vinegar, put the flower without being dried.
For garlic vinegar: take four pints of white vinegar for one ounce of garlic, twelve cloves, and one nutmeg cut into pieces.

After having bunged it, make a hole in the top of the barrel above the jable, large enough to insert a large funnel.
Pour in through the funnel two pints of good vinegar.
Eight days later, add one pint of clean wine suitable for making vinegar.
Every eight days add one pint of wine until the barrel is half full, then you may add more.
You must take care that the wine is always of the same strength as the first that you put in, because if it were weaker, the increase you would make would not have the same strength.
Your barrel being full and the vinegar in its state, withdraw two-thirds of it which you put in another vessel.
Then you will gradually return wine to the barrel as described above; by this means you always have vinegar.

For white vinegar: put ten pints of vinegar on the fire and let it boil until it is reduced to eight; then have it distilled in an alembic, putting in more or less according to the quantity you desire.
For rose vinegar: dry an ounce of musk roses in the sun for two days, which you will put in one pint of vinegar; place the roses and vinegar in the sun for fifteen days in a well-stopped bottle.
For tarragon, elder, or carnation vinegar: make the same way; for orange flower vinegar, put the flower without being dried.
For garlic vinegar: take four pints of white vinegar for one ounce of garlic, twelve cloves, and one nutmeg cut into pieces.

steps: Trim your filet as in previous recipes
Lard it with large lardons containing spices, a little thyme, two minced or crushed bay leaves, and fine salt
Tie the filet securely with string
Place bacon strips, two veal slices, and two beef slices in the bottom of a casserole with vegetables such as carrots, onions, and a bouquet garni
Place your filet in the casserole and cover with bacon strips
Add half a bottle or three quarters of a bottle of Malaga wine, depending on the size of your filet, and half a spoonful of broth
Bring to a boil; once it releases some broth, simmer gently over low heat for two and a half hours
When cooked, strain the cooking liquid through a silk sieve
Add three spoonfuls of espagnole sauce and pour the strained liquid into your sauce
Reduce to a glaze, meaning you produce only enough juice to sauce your filet
Remove and untie the filet, glaze it, and pour your reduction underneath
Alternatively, you may cook this filet by placing it between bacon strips with vegetables moistened with Malaga wine and a little broth

title: Filet d'Aloyau aux Cornichons (Sirloin Filet with Gherkins)
description: Prepared with gherkins, lard, and espagnole.
steps: Trim your filet as you would for braising
Lard it with fine lard and place it on a spit, then arrange it on your serving platter in such a way that it is not too long so your dish can contain it
Prepare your gherkins cut into small sticks
Take six spoonfuls of espagnole sauce and add three spoonfuls of vinegar, a little salt, and fine pepper to dominate; add eight spoonfuls of consommé
Reduce everything by half, skim and degrease your sauce
When reduced, strain it through cheesecloth, add your gherkins, and keep this sauce hot without boiling
After your filet has been on the spit for an hour and a half, place it on your platter with your sauce underneath
If you lack espagnole, make a light roux, moisten it with stock or broth, season as above, add your gherkins cut into thin slices, salt, and fine pepper

title: Filet d'Aloyau Braisé (Braised Sirloin Fillet)
description: Prepared with fat, bay leaf, and lard.
steps: Remove the sirloin fillet and remove all the fat from it
Lay your fillet on the table on the side where the skin is; make sure the meat lies flat on the table with your hand

Take a large sharp knife; place the blade between the skin and the meat so well that by moving your knife back and forth, as if you were lifting a strip of lard, you separate the skin with the fillet and it becomes well unified and trimmed
If any skin remains, you must remove it by sliding the blade of your knife as close as possible to the skin to avoid hollows in your fillet
When it is well trimmed, take large lardons in which you put a little thyme, a little crushed or finely chopped bay leaf, a little quatre épices, and a little salt and pepper
Lard your fillet and tie it, giving it the shape you want
Put in the bottom of your pot strips of lard, slices of veal and beef, four or six onions, one of which is studded with three cloves, two bay leaves, a little thyme, a bouquet of parsley and chives
Place your fillet in your pot where your braising base is marked; cover it with lard and place a few pieces of meat around it
Pour in two large spoonfuls of bouillon and very little salt
Bring your braise to a boil, then place it over a gentle fire to simmer for two and a half hours
Take the cooking liquid in which your fillet has cooked; pass it through a silk sieve and reduce it
When your fillet is drained, untie it and glaze it
Dress it on your serving dish and pour the reduced cooking liquid over it

If you do not have everything needed to braise your fillet, trim it and lard it with large lard; put your trimmings in the bottom of your pot; tie your fillet; place it on your trimmings; add your carrots, onions, bouquet of aromatics, two spoonfuls of bouillon; if you have none, add water and salt, not too much so that you can use the cooking liquid for what you have to do; when it is cooked, serve it as above: make sure your fillet looks good and is well seasoned

title: Filet de Bœuf à la Conti (Beef Filet à la Conti)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and carrots.

ingredients.name: deux feuilles de laurier (two bay leaves)
ingredients.sourceText: deux feuilles de laurier (two bay leaves)

ingredients.name: bouquet de persil et de ciboules (bouquet of parsley and chives)
ingredients.sourceText: bouquet de persil et de ciboules (bouquet of parsley and chives)

steps: Lard your filet as the previous one and lard it with large lard underneath
Tie it in such a way that it forms a spiral
Butter the bottom of your casserole and place your filet in it with four carrots, five onions, two bay leaves, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and three cloves
Add a spoonful of aspic or broth and a sheet of buttered paper cut in a round shape
Bring your filet to a boil; when it releases some broth, place it over low heat and place coals also on the lid of your casserole
Check from time to time, ensuring your filet takes on a beautiful color
It takes two hours to cook, and the cooking liquid must reduce to a glaze so your filet is glazed when you remove it
Remove your vegetables from the casserole along with the fat
Add four spoonfuls of espagnole and one of consommé to your casserole and detach the glaze from your filet
Strain your sauce through cheesecloth and pour it under your filet

If you lack sauce, glaze your filet with the glaze in your casserole; add about a teaspoon of flour that you dissolve with your glaze; add also a glass of broth; bring your sauce to a boil and strain it through cheesecloth; pour it over your filet and ensure your sauce has good seasoning

title: Filets de Chevreuil (Roe Deer Loins)
description: Prepared with roe, vinegar, and bay leaves.
steps: Remove the two loins from your roe deer
Trim them as explained for beef loin

Lard them and place them in a terrine with two glasses of vinegar, salt, fine pepper, four bay leaves, six cloves, six or eight branches of thyme, four onions cut into slices, a small handful of parsley in branches, and a few whole chives
Leave to marinate forty-eight hours or longer if you have time
When you wish to serve them, remove them from your marinade and prepare them properly
Spread strips of lard in a casserole with a few slices of roe deer, three carrots, three onions, two cloves, two bay leaves, and a little thyme
Arrange your loins in spirals or otherwise
Place them on your seasoning, cover them with buttered paper
Pour over them half a bottle of white wine and as much bouillon with a little salt
Let them simmer over heat above and below for one hour
At the moment of serving, drain them, remove the string or skewers if there are any
Glaze them and dress them on your platter

Serve a piquant sauce underneath; if you have none, make a light roux that you will moisten with the cooking liquid from your loins, add a little juice so your sauce has good color, three spoonfuls of vinegar, salt, and fine pepper
Reduce your sauce by half so it takes on flavor
You can also roast these same loins on a spit if you do not wish to braise them

description: Prepared with pheasant, lard, and veal.
steps: Remove eight fillets from the pheasant
Set aside the tenderloin fillets which you will sauté and arrange in the middle
Trim your fillets and lard them with fine lard
Place lard strips in a saucepan with the trimmings of your pheasants, several slices of veal, two carrots, four onions, two bay leaves, two cloves
Arrange your fillets well so they keep a beautiful form
Place over them a round of buttered paper, one glass of white wine and two glasses of consommé, a little salt
There should be no liquid over your fillets, but liquid up to the larding
Place them on the fire one hour before serving
When they boil, place them over gentle heat, and much heat on the lid so they glaze
At the moment of serving, drain them, glaze them, pass through silk sieve the liquid in which they cooked
Reduce it almost to a glaze
Pour over it three spoonfuls of espagnole sauce which you boil with your reduction
Pass it through cheesecloth and arrange your fillets flat on croûtons passed in butter and three lines thick

Pour your sauce underneath; you can also place lard strips on a baking pan, and your fillets with a glass of white wine, salt, a little coarse pepper, a little aromatic spices, a round of buttered paper, and put them in the oven or under the oven

steps: Cut the cucumbers into thin slices as fine as possible
Place them in a pot with {{source-1}} and salt, and marinate for two hours, turning them from time to time

Heat without boiling
Season with salt and coarse pepper
Serve. The fillets should be the leftovers from roasted rabbits that have been removed from the table.

title: Filets de Lièvre Marinés Sautés (Marinated Sautéed Hare Fillets)
description: Prepared with hare, chives, and vinegar.
steps: Trim and lard your fillets as in the previous recipe.
Place them in a terrine with salt, pepper, two laurel leaves, thyme, parsley sprigs, whole chives, and a large glass of vinegar.
Leave them to marinate for up to eight days.
When you wish to serve them, remove them from the marinade, trim them, drain them, and shape them as desired.
Place them in your sauté pan and coat them with warm butter so they are bathed in it.
At the moment of service, place your sauté pan over a high heat so your fillets do not sweat.
When they are stiffened on one side, turn them.
When you feel your fillets are firm to the touch, remove them, drain them, and arrange them on your plate.
Place a poivrade sauce underneath.
If you have no sauce, heat your butter until what is in the sauté pan begins to stick.
Remove three quarters of the butter.
Add a small spoonful of flour, which you stir with your butter.
Add some of the herbs from your marinade, a small pot-spoonful of bouillon, half of the vinegar that marinated your fillets, and enough pepper to dominate.
Reduce your sauce by half or more if it is too thin.
Strain it through a sieve into another pan.
Check the seasoning for salt and place it under your fillets.

description: Prepared with partridge, partridges, and sauce.
steps: Put eight partridges on the spit three-quarters of an hour before serving
When they are cooked, still slightly undercooked (in their own juice), remove them from the spit
Correctly remove the fillets
On the platter, arrange a glazed crouton of approximately the same shape as your fillets, but flat

Pound some kidneys from your partridges and put them in your roux
Moisten with bouillon, half a glass of white wine, and a bay leaf
Reduce by half
Skim it and strain through a fine sieve
Squeeze your bitter orange into it as explained

When it has released three or four boils, add parsley chopped the size of half an egg of very good butter

title: Foie de Veau en Crépine (Calf's Liver in Caul Fat)
description: Prepared with liver, onions, and beef fat.
steps: Cut two large onions into small dice and put them in a saucepan with butter, cooking over the fire until done
Chop one calf's liver finely with three quarterons of beef fat

Put the chopped liver into a mortar with the cooked onion, dried bread crumb that has been dried over the fire with half a septier of milk, chopped parsley, chives, and mushrooms, salt, coarse pepper, four egg yolks, and four beaten egg whites
Pound everything together
Take a medium saucepan and place lard slices on the bottom
Place a pig's caul on top that you have soaked for half an hour in fresh water and well pressed with your hands to remove the water
Put all the forcemeat into the caul and seal all the edges with beaten egg to hold them together
Cover the saucepan with a sheet of paper and a lid
Cook over low heat between two beds of hot ashes for half an hour
Drain off the fat and gently pull the caul onto a white cloth so as not to break it, and wipe off the remaining fat
Arrange on the serving dish and put a good somewhat thin sauce on top where you have put half a spoonful of verjuice

steps: Cut a calf's liver into very thin fillets
Chop finely parsley, chives, mushrooms, half a clove of garlic, two shallots, half a bay leaf, thyme, and basil chopped like powder
Take a medium saucepan and put a layer of calf's liver fillets on the bottom
Season on top with salt, coarse pepper, fine oil, and a little of all your fine herbs

Cook over low heat for one hour

Degrease the sauce and put in a very small piece of beurre manié made with flour and half a spoonful of verjuice or a drop of vinegar
Thicken the sauce over the fire turning it with a spoon; if it was too thin, add a little juice
Put the liver in the sauce to heat it and arrange on the serving dish

Season on top with salt, coarse pepper, fine oil, and a little of all your fine herbs
Continue in this manner until you have used all the liver, seasoning each layer as you did the first
Cook over low heat for one hour
Remove the liver from the saucepan with a skimmer
Degrease the sauce and put in a very small piece of beurre manié made with flour and half a spoonful of verjuice or a drop of vinegar
Thicken the sauce over the fire turning it with a spoon; if it was too thin, add a little juice
Put the liver in the sauce to heat it and arrange on the serving dish

title: Foie de Veau étouffé (Braised Calf's Liver)
description: Prepared with liver, lard, and carrots.
steps: Take a calf's liver and lard it with thick lardons.
Season it with four spices, chopped parsley and chives, pepper, salt.
When your liver is larded, put lard strips in a braising pan or casserole.
Put your liver with four carrots, four onions (one of which is studded with three cloves), three bay leaves, a little thyme, a bouquet of parsley and chives, salt.
Moisten your liver with a bottle of white wine.
Cover it with lard strips and a round of paper.
Put it on a stove.
When it comes to a boil, place it on another braising pan with fire on the cover.
Let it simmer for two hours and you can serve it.
Add about four spoonfuls to degrease of poivrade sauce; strain the cooking liquid from your liver and add four spoonfuls of it.
Reduce your sauce by half and pour it under your liver.
If you do not have poivrade sauce, make a small roux; pass through a silk sieve the cooking liquid in which your liver cooked; moisten your roux with it.
Your sauce must be thin so you can reduce it by half.
Degrease it and place it under your liver.

description: Prepared with carrots, onions, and bay leaves.
steps: Soak the mesentery well in cold water

Serve with the vinegar sauce

steps: Cook a calf sweetbread with water

Moisten with a glass of bouillon and one spoonful of vinegar

Thicken this sauce over the fire so it is somewhat thick and put it on the sweetbread

title: Frangipane (Almond Cream)
description: Prepared with almond, almonds, and candied orange.

ingredients.name: Butter the size of an egg
ingredients.sourceText: Butter the size of an egg

ingredients.name: One bitter almond per six sweet almonds
ingredients.sourceText: One bitter almond per six sweet almonds

steps: Put in a saucepan five spoonfuls of flour, which you will mix with five eggs
Pour in one pint of milk, butter the size of an egg, and a little salt
Put your mixture over the fire
Stir the frangipane constantly without leaving it until it has boiled for ten minutes
Be careful it does not brown
When it is cooked, let it cool in a bowl
Then crush some almonds; for every six, use one bitter almond; crush some macarons until they are a fine powder
Add a little candied orange flower and powdered sugar in large enough quantity that it is a good sugar
Mix all with your mixture
When the frangipane is well worked with a wooden spoon, if it is too thick, add one or two eggs with your puff pastry
Make tarts and small cakes of all sorts and in all fashions
If you want your cream to be pistacio flavored, when it is cold, put pistachios instead of almonds
As this would not give enough color, add a little spinach green; do not use macarons or orange flower, but rather three bitter almonds and sugar

title: Fricassée de Poulet (Chicken Fricassee)
description: Prepared with fat, bouillon or water, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: About a quarter pound of butter
ingredients.sourceText: About a quarter pound of butter

ingredients.name: A bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: A bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Flame the chicken and disjoint it as correctly as possible, lifting the members without hacking or skinning them so they retain a beautiful form
Cut the end of the thigh at the side of the leg; break and remove the bone to the joint so your thigh has a beautiful form
Warm about a quarter pound of butter in a saucepan
Arrange the thighs, then the wings, breast, kidneys and the rest on top
Put your fricassee on the fire and stiffen the chicken members at the bottom of your saucepan
After they have remained an instant on the fire, sauté them
When they are all stiffened, pour a spoon of flour that you will mix with your chicken and butter
Add a pot spoon of bouillon; if you have none, moisten it with water
Add salt, coarse pepper, a bay leaf, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and mushrooms
Bring it to a boil, stirring constantly
Skim it and let it go to a high fire
One hour is sufficient to cook your fricassee, unless your chicken is tough
When it is three-quarters cooked, degrease it
Add small onions, all equal and well cleaned, as you judge appropriate
Once your fricassee is cooked, remove the bouquet and bay leaf
Add a liaison of three egg yolks; take care that it does not boil
Add lemon juice if you wish

title: Fromage de Cochon (Pork Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with bay leaf, garlic, and shallots.
steps: Take a well-cleaned pig head and bone it completely
Remove all the meat and lard without cutting the skin; cut the meat into very thin fillets
Do the same with the lard
Place lean meat on one plate, fat on another
Cut the ears into fillets as well
Season all meat on both sides with salt, coarse pepper, thyme, bay leaf, basil, six cloves, two pinches of coriander, and half a nutmeg, all finely chopped
Add two minced garlic cloves and four minced shallots
Add half a handful of parsley leaves left whole
Place the pig head skin in a round pot
Arrange all your meat fillets, adding a bit of vinegar and some ham slices if available, with neatly arranged parsley leaves
Continue this layering until complete

description: Prepared with double cream or cream, egg yolk, and orange or lime or citron.

steps: Take one chopine of double cream or other good cream, one half-setier of milk, one egg yolk, and three quarterons of sugar
Bring to five or six boils and remove from the fire
Add several essences such as orange flowers, bergamot, sweet lime or citron
Place the mixture in your tin mold and set it to freeze on ice

When your cheese is frozen and you are ready to serve, have hot water in a cauldron, dip the mold of the cheese in it to make it detach, and dress it in the dish; it must be eaten at once

title: Galantine de Dindon (Turkey Galantine)
description: Prepared with turkey, chicken or veal or meat, and lard.
steps: Singe your turkey; make sure it has good meat and is well nourished
Begin to bone it through the back; be careful not to damage the breast
When it is entirely boned and the sinews of the thighs are removed, lift some of the meat from the breast half an inch from the skin
Do the same for the thighs
Put with the meat you have cut from the top of your turkey that of two or three chickens, or simply veal or other meat; this is optional
If you have two pounds of meat, put two pounds of the fattest lard possible; chop everything together
Add salt, pepper, four spices, fine herbs
If you wish, when your forcemeat is finely chopped, season medium lardons with pounded aromatics, salt, and pepper, and lard the meat of your turkey
Make a layer of forcemeat one inch thick, which you press down well and evenly
Put on this layer of forcemeat truffles cut lengthwise, scarlet tongue, lard lardons, the filets of your turkey and poultry, foie gras if you have it
Add another layer of forcemeat, and as before, truffles, tongue, lardons, etc., until you have no more forcemeat; perform the same procedure
When your forcemeat is used up, roll your turkey so that it contains all the forcemeat without any escaping from any side
With a trussing needle and string, sew the meat together as it was in its original form
Give your galantine an elongated shape; cover it with lard slices, a little salt
Wrap it in canvas cloth into which you put four or five bay leaves
Tie your two ends and tie your galantine on top of the canvas so it keeps its shape
Put lard slices in a braising pan, your galantine on top

Add two veal knuckles, six carrots, six onions, a strong bouquet of parsley and chives, the scraps of your turkey, four bay leaves, a little thyme, three cloves, three pot spoonfuls of bouillon, more if your piece is large
Put it on the fire and simmer for three hours

title: Garbure aux Laitues (Garbure with Lettuce)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and bread.
steps: Blanch the lettuces for half an hour, keeping them whole
Let them cool, press them, and tie them with string
Put slices of veal and lard at the bottom of a saucepan
Add the lettuces and cover them with lard along with two or three carrots, three onions, and two cloves
Moisten with bouillon and simmer for an hour and a half until cooked
Drain and cut lengthwise into slices
Make a layer of thinly sliced bread in your dish, then a layer of lettuce, continuing until full
Pour the bouillon from the lettuce over it without degreasing, but after passing through a silk sieve
Put the dish on the fire to simmer until it has a golden crust
Spare the salt due to reduction; add a little coarse pepper to each layer
Before serving, degrease your garbure and serve bouillon in a separate vessel

steps: Cut the onions in half from the top to the other end
Cut half of them into four or five parts until they form half a circle
Be careful not to include the head or the tail
When all your onions are cut this way, take half a pound of butter or more according to the quantity of your onions
Fry them in the butter enough so they are well browned
Take bread cut into very thin slices
Make a layer of bread and a layer of onions
Put on each layer a little coarse pepper until your dish is full
Drizzle with broth and simmer enough so the gratin forms without letting it burn, which would give it acidity
Your soup must be almost dry
Put broth in a vessel and serve it so people can add it to their plate
Pay attention to salt because of the reduction

steps: Take three of the freshest eggs you can find and dilute them with as much flour as they can absorb, chopped green citron, orange flower water, and fine sugar
Dilute all together and then add a little more than one half-setier of cream, until the batter is somewhat liquid
When your batter is ready, heat the waffle iron over a fire and rub it inside with candle wax to prevent the waffles from sticking

When it is cooked on one side, turn it over to the other side and remove it then to place it on a wooden roller
Bend them all while hot, and when they are all made, put them in a dry place until you serve them
You can keep them for several days if you keep them in a drying room where they will not soften

title: Gelée d'Oranges (Orange Jelly)
description: Prepared with oranges, lemons, and isinglass.
steps: Take 10 oranges and 3 lemons
Zest 3 oranges very lightly, removing the peel in small portions with a knife
Place the zest in a casserole
Press the 10 oranges and 3 lemons over the zests
Clarify half a pound of sugar
Place the orange juice and zests with the clarified sugar brought almost to hard crack stage
Heat with the sugar and juice of oranges
Pass through fine cloth

Add a decoction of 3 sticks of isinglass made by beating well and placing in small pieces in a casserole with 3 spoons of water, simmering for two hours, then passing through cheesecloth without straining or pressing
Mix the isinglass with the warm preparation
Amalgamate well the isinglass and juice
Pour the jelly into small pots and place on ice or in a cool place
When the jelly is completely set, remove from ice
7 small pots suffice for an entremets

title: Gelées pour les Malades (Jellies for the Sick)
description: Prepared with chicken, veal, and lemon.

ingredients.name: one chicken, flamed, emptied, and plucked
ingredients.sourceText: one chicken, flamed, emptied, and plucked

ingredients.name: a veal knuckle of about one and a half pounds

ingredients.name: a slice of green lemon, skin removed

ingredients.name: two or three grains of salt

ingredients.name: a very small piece of cinnamon

ingredients.name: three eggs with whites and yolks and shells

steps: Put in a pot a chicken that you have flamed, emptied, and plucked, a veal knuckle of about one and a half pounds, and two pints of water.
Bring them to boil and skim well, then simmer on very low heat for three hours.
Degrease your broth well and pass it through a fine tamis, put it in a casserole on a good stove with a slice of green lemon, skin removed.
If you have no lemon, put in a few drops of white vinegar, a quarter pound of sugar, two or three grains of salt, two pinches of coriander, a very small piece of cinnamon.
Boil for a quarter hour, and put in three eggs with whites and yolks and shells, boil gently while stirring often until your jelly is clear and reduced to about three half-setiers.
Pass it through a white cloth that is moistened, press it well so that it does not smell of lye and no water remains.
Put your jelly in the vessels where it must stay, let it set in a cool place or on ice.

title: Gigot de Mouton aux Légumes Glacés (Leg of Mutton with Glazed Vegetables)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, vegetables, and bouillon.
steps: Trim the leg of mutton of its fat and the end of the shank; truss it and place in a pot with good bouillon
Turn the half head of cabbage and the dozen root vegetables cut in rounds; add six large onions and three celery stalks
Blanch everything together for half a quarter hour
Remove and refresh in fresh water, press out any water, and truss the cabbage and celery
Cook all these vegetables with the leg of mutton
When everything is cooked, remove the leg of mutton and vegetables to a platter and wipe away any grease with a white cloth
Arrange the leg of mutton on the serving platter with vegetables around it
Take the bouillon used to cook the leg of mutton, degrease it and pass through a sieve, reduce it to two spoonfuls to make your glaze
Lightly glaze the leg of mutton and vegetables

Put clear coulis in the casserole where the glaze was reduced to detach what remains, pass this sauce through a sieve to make it clearer, season it well, and serve over the vegetables without touching the glaze
