title: Gigot de Mouton de sept heures (Seven-Hour Leg of Mutton)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, mutton, and lard.
steps: Debone the leg of mutton halfway up the shank
Season with lardons, salt, coarse pepper, thyme and bay leaf, all pounded
Lard the interior of the leg, ensuring the lardons do not protrude on top
Restore the leg to its original shape and tie it with twine so that the deboning is not apparent

Place lard strips in the bottom of a braising pot, followed by ham slices, crushed bones, mutton slices, four carrots, six onions, three bay leaves, a little thyme, three cloves, and a bouquet of parsley and chives
Add one spoonful of broth and place all this mixture above the leg of mutton
Cover the leg with lard and a buttered paper to cover it
Place the leg in the coals to cook for seven hours if it is large, at a gentle fire
Also place coals on the lid of the braising pot
When ready to serve, drain the cooking liquid, untie the leg, glaze it, and serve with the reduced cooking liquid in which it cooked

title: Gigot à la Royale (Leg of Mutton à la Royale)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, veal, and mushrooms.
steps: Braise a leg of mutton in the same manner as mutton with cabbage
Prepare a ragout: soak veal sweetbread in tepid water, blanch for half a quarter-hour in boiling water, cool in fresh water, and cut into large dice; remove the cartilage
Put the sweetbread in a saucepan with mushrooms cut the same way, sauté over fire with a bouquet of parsley, chives, two cloves, and half a clove of garlic
Add a pinch of flour, then moisten with half stock and half bouillon in equal parts
Cook on very low heat, season with salt and coarse pepper
When cooking is almost complete, skim off fat and add small eggs that have been blanched in boiling water beforehand
Remove eggs to fresh water to take off the small skin
After they have boiled half a quarter-hour in the ragout, add lemon juice or a small splash of vinegar
Serve under the leg of mutton

Alternative for small eggs: hard boil two eggs, take the yolks and place in a mortar with half a pinch of salt, pound them, and add one raw yolk; mix well, remove to a table dusted with a little flour, roll into the shape of a small sausage, cut into very small equal pieces, roll each piece in slightly floured hands to round them, and place on a plate as you go; put them in boiling water to cook for an instant, cool in fresh water, and drain on a sieve before putting in the ragout

Boil for one hour on low heat until the sauce is reduced by half
Pass through a sieve, then add a finely chopped hard egg and a pinch of blanched parsley, finely chopped, as much as a nut of butter kneaded with flour
Thicken over fire and serve over the leg of mutton

When your sauce boils, place it on the corner of the stove so it boils gently for 2 or 3 hours until your meats are cooked
When skimming and boiling, be careful to skim well what you place on the fire and wipe the interior of your casserole beforehand to avoid cloudy sauces
Ensure your sauce is neither too brown nor too pale, neither too clear nor too thick, and that it has a gentle salt

title: Grande Sauce (Great Sauce)
description: A sauce made with veal, consommé, and carrots.

ingredients.name: The underside of the veal round (four or one piece according to desired quantity of sauce)
ingredients.sourceText: The underside of the veal round (four or one piece according to desired quantity of sauce)

ingredients.name: Four or five large turned carrots
ingredients.sourceText: Four or five large turned carrots

ingredients.name: Four or five onions, one of which is studded with two cloves
ingredients.sourceText: Four or five onions, one of which is studded with two cloves

ingredients.name: A bouquet of parsley and chives
ingredients.sourceText: A bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Take the underside of the veal round (four or one piece according to the quantity of sauce you want)
Put them in a large casserole with two pot-spoonfuls of consommé
Make them sweat over a somewhat hot fire
Be careful to remove as much foam as possible
Also be careful to wipe with a white cloth what sticks to the inside of your casserole so your sauce is not cloudy
When the consommé is reduced, prick your pieces of veal with your knife to draw out the juice
Put your casserole on a gentle fire so your meat and glaze attach slowly
When the glaze at the bottom of your casserole becomes blonde, remove it from heat and leave it covered
After ten minutes, fill it with grand bouillon in which you have put four or five large turned carrots and three large onions
Let your pieces of veal simmer for two hours
During this time, take the four noix and put them in a casserole with four or five turned carrots and four or five onions, one of which is studded with two cloves
Put two pot-spoonfuls of consommé in it
Put the casserole with your noix on a somewhat hot fire so the moistening reduces and becomes glaze
When you see your glaze is more than blonde, transfer the moistening from your pieces of veal that have boiled for two hours and pour it over your noix
Let them detach slowly, then make them start, that is to say boil
Make a roux and dilute it with the moistening in your casserole
When your roux is well dissolved, pour it over your veal noix
Add some mushrooms, a bouquet of parsley and chives, and two bay leaves
Be careful to foam well when it begins to boil
Skim again when you bind your sauce with your roux
Try to make your sauce neither too clear nor too thick; if it is too thick, add some moistening; if it is not thick enough, dilute a little roux and put it in your sauce
When your sauce has boiled an hour and a half, degrease it, that is to say remove the grease found on the back of your sauce
When your meat is cooked, pass your sauce through a sieve

title: Grande Sauce (Large Brown Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef shoulder, veal, and trimmings.

ingredients.name: 1 or 2 pounds of beef shoulder (according to the size of the sauce)

ingredients.name: a large bouquet of parsley and chives

steps: Place all the meat and vegetables into a casserole
Add one pot spoon full of water
Place your meats on a fairly hot fire
When there is almost no moisture left in your casserole, move it to a gentle fire so that the glaze at the bottom of your casserole colors without burning
When it is a dark blonde and your glaze is brown, moisten it with water if you do not have broth
Add a large bouquet of parsley and chives, 2 bay leaves, 2 cloves, and mushrooms if you have them
Leave your meat to cook well skimmed and salted for three hours
After, pass the juice of your meat through a silk sieve
Make a roux and dilute it with your moistening liquid, and let your sauce boil for one hour on low heat
Degrease it, then pass it through cheesecloth or a horsehair sieve if you lack cheesecloth
Ensure your sauce is neither too pale nor too brown, neither too clear nor too thick, and that it is flavorful and well-salted

title: Grenouilles en Fricassée de Poulets (Frogs in Chicken Fricassee Style)
description: Prepared with mushrooms, white wine, and bouillon.
steps: Put the frogs in boiling water and let them boil a little
Remove to fresh water and drain
Place them in a casserole with mushrooms, a bouquet of parsley, ciboule, one clove of garlic, two cloves, and a piece of butter
Pass over the fire two or three times and add a good pinch of flour
Moisten with a glass of white wine and a little bouillon, add salt and coarse pepper
Cook for a quarter hour and reduce to a short sauce
Add a liaison of three egg yolks mixed with a little cream and a small pinch of finely chopped parsley
Bind without boiling

description: Prepared with onion, garlic, and shallots.
steps: Place the raw frogs in a marinade of equal parts water and vinegar with parsley, whole ciboule, onion slices, two garlic cloves, two shallots, three cloves, bay leaf, thyme, and basil for one hour

title: Grives aux Cerises (Thrushes with Cherry Garnish)
description: Prepared with forcemeat, shallots, and white wine.
steps: Pluck the thrushes whole; singe them lightly; debone them starting from the back; once well deboned, take the livers and pound them with the back of the knife; mix them with fine forcemeat, a little pounded aromatic herbs, and coarse pepper

Fill your thrushes with this forcemeat, but first pass a leg through the middle of the body, having cut off a large piece so that it represents the tail of a cherry; once the body is filled with forcemeat, bring the flesh together with a needle and secure it
Place your thrushes in a casserole with salt and coarse pepper; warm a piece of butter and pour it over your thrushes

Half an hour before serving, put them on the fire to simmer in the butter; at the moment of serving, drain them and remove the strings holding them; arrange them on the plate like cherries in a compote dish

Sauce them with an italienne; if you do not have any, reduce the juice your thrushes have rendered; remove three-quarters of the butter; add a little parsley and finely chopped shallots, which you will pass a moment in your butter; add about half a spoonful of flour, the equivalent of half a glass of white wine, and as much bouillon; bring your sauce to a boil a few times; degrease it; check that it is well bound and properly seasoned; use it for your thrushes
